subject: math

objective.text: Subtract with the standard algorithm, regrouping up to three times. Solve word problems with tape diagrams.

explanations.title: Regroup twice
explanations.text: Check each column from right to left. Every column that lacks units needs 1 unit unbundled from the column on its left.

explanations.title: Zero in the unbundling column
explanations.text: If the next column on the left has none, look one more column left. Unbundle there, then pass the units down.

explanations.title: Start in any ready column
explanations.text: After the top number is ready, you can subtract in any column. Name the units as you subtract.

explanations.title: Check by adding
explanations.text: Add the difference to the part you subtracted. The sum should be the whole.

explanations.title: Choose a variable
explanations.text: A letter stands for the unknown number in the tape diagram. The letter can match the thing you find.

examples.title: 22,397 minus 3,745
examples.text: The hundreds column has 3, which is not enough for 7. Unbundle 1 thousand. Now there are 13 hundreds. The thousands column has 1, which is not enough for 3. Unbundle 1 ten thousand. The answer is 18,652.

examples.title: 210,290 minus 45,720
examples.text: The hundreds column lacks units. There are no thousands to unbundle, so use the ten thousands. The answer is 164,570.

examples.title: 859,239 minus 272,650
examples.text: Regroup three times. The answer is 586,589 dollars.

hints.text: Multiply the number by the unit. Then write it in standard form.
Subtract the matching units. Then write the answer.
Think about how many centimeters make one meter.
The amount is 10 times as much. Undo that by dividing by 10.
Find the whole and the part you know. Subtract to find the other part.
Compare the top digit with the bottom digit in this column.
Unbundle 1 unit from the column on the left. It becomes 10 of this unit.
Line up the places. Check each column. Unbundle when a column lacks units.
Add the difference to the part you subtracted. Do you get the whole?

assets_required.why_this_method: The lesson uses place value disks and tape diagrams on paper. The child cannot draw them.
assets_required.description: A vertical subtraction with place value columns up to hundred thousands. The child checks each column, unbundles through zeros, subtracts, and checks by adding.
must_show_exactly: Columns in order: hundred thousands, ten thousands, thousands, hundreds, tens, ones
A top number and a bottom number lined up
A ready check for each column
Unbundling that can pass through a zero column
A tape diagram with the whole, the known part and a variable
A check row that adds the difference and the known part
assets_required.interaction: Child checks each column, unbundles when a column is not ready, then subtracts and checks by adding.
assets_required.alt_text: A vertical subtraction with unbundling through a zero and a tape diagram.
assets_required.generation_caption: A clean vertical subtraction with six labeled columns, small crossed-out renames above, and a tape diagram beside it. [Build by code]
assets_required.review_notes: Source charts are blank pictures. Build from the printed numbers.
